Vocational Skills Training Implementation Notice
This notice sets out the binding arrangements for delivering the vocational skills
training programme during the 2025 cycle. It applies to all training sites, contracted
instructors and enrolled trainees, and replaces prior informal guidance. The
programme runs for 12 weeks with 24 sessions and 48 teaching hours, and must be
delivered within the cost and output envelope recorded in the annexed schedule.
Site coordinators are accountable for compliance with every clause below.
1 Programme Scope and Training Objectives
The programme targets practical competency in the designated trade areas and is
limited to trainees who meet the entry criteria. Its objectives are to raise measurable
skill attainment, reduce workplace error rates and prepare trainees for assessment.
Training content must align with the approved curriculum and may not be
substituted without written approval. Each site must deliver the full 48 teaching
hours and document attendance against the session plan.
Supporting records are presented in Figure 1.
Figure 1: Programme delivery parameters and site allocation
1.1 Delivery Schedule and Site Allocation
Delivery is organised across 4 training sites, each operating the same 12 week
schedule to preserve comparability. The schedule fixes 24 sessions per cohort, with
no more than two sessions in any single day. Site allocation follows trainee residence
and equipment availability; transfers require coordinator approval. Any deviation
from the published timetable must be recorded and reported within 2 working days
so that central monitoring remains accurate.

1.1.1 Session Planning and Instructor Duties
Instructors must prepare session plans that map each of the 24 sessions to a
curriculum unit and an assessment checkpoint. Plans are submitted before the
cohort starts and are subject to review within 5 working days. Instructors record
attendance, practical observations and remedial actions in the session log. They
must also verify that safety briefings precede any equipment use and that trainees
sign the attendance register at each session.
Supporting records are presented in Table 1.
1.1.1.1 Practical Demonstration Standards
Table 1: Instructor session planning and review duties
Practical demonstrations must follow the approved task checklist and be observed
by a second instructor where the task carries safety risk. Each demonstration is
scored against defined criteria, and any trainee scoring below the pass threshold
receives a documented retake. Demonstrations may not be compressed to recover
lost time. Records of demonstration outcomes are retained for audit and must
distinguish observed performance from instructor expectation.
1.1.1.2 Assessment and Feedback Cycle
Assessment comprises a mid programme check and a final practical examination,
each contributing to the overall result. Feedback is returned within 5 working days of
each assessment so trainees can act on it before the next checkpoint. Assessors
must use the standard rubric and record evidence for every criterion. Appeals are
lodged within 2 working days and are handled by a reviewer not involved in the
original assessment.
1.1.2 Attendance and Completion Rules
Trainees must attend at least the minimum number of sessions specified in the
cohort agreement to be eligible for completion. Absences are recorded with cause

and may be made up only through approved catch up sessions. Completion
certificates are issued after the final assessment and attendance verification.
Coordinators reconcile attendance registers against session logs before certifying
completion, and unresolved discrepancies are escalated to the programme office.
1.2 Resource and Cost Control
Each site operates within the cost allocation shown in the resource schedule, and
expenditure is reviewed monthly against the approved envelope. Equipment,
materials and instructor time are the principal cost lines. Sites must report variances
promptly and may not commit expenditure beyond their allocation without prior
approval. The programme office consolidates site returns and compares them with
the planned output and cost profile before releasing the next tranche of funding.
Supporting records are presented in Figure 2.
Figure 2: Cost control checks by site
2 Monitoring, Reporting and Quality Assurance
Monitoring combines site visits, record checks and trainee feedback. The programme
office reviews 240 trainee records per cycle to verify attendance, assessment and
completion data. Quality assurance focuses on consistency of assessment and
adherence to session plans. Findings are graded and tracked to closure, and
recurring issues trigger a targeted review. Reports must separate verified
observations from inferred causes and must not present correlation as proof of
effect.
2.1 Data Collection and Record Keeping
Sites maintain a single register of trainees, sessions, assessments and completions.
Data is entered within 2 working days of each event and reconciled monthly.
Records must be accurate, legible and retained for the audit period. Personal data is
handled according to the privacy rules in the cohort agreement. The programme
SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT | RESEARCH PROTOTYPE
office may request extracts at any time and will compare them with site returns to
identify gaps.
2.1.1 Performance Indicators and Review Cycle
Performance is tracked through output, cost and balance indicators recorded for
each cycle. The review cycle compares actual delivery with the planned profile and
documents explanations for variances. Indicators are simulated planning values and
are not audited financial statements. Reviewers must state clearly when an indicator
reflects observation rather than a causal claim, and must avoid attributing changes
to the programme without supporting evidence.
2.1.1.1 Output, Cost and Balance Records
The annexed records show output, cost and balance for the recent cycles. Output
rose across the period while cost increased more slowly, producing a widening
balance. These figures are simulated planning indicators used for internal
comparison only. Reviewers should read them alongside delivery records and must
not treat the trend as evidence that the programme caused the change. Any
variance explanation requires corroborating site documentation.

Figure 3: Indicator review and variance handling steps
Site coordinators should confirm that the session plan references the correct
curriculum unit before the cohort begins, and that any substitution is approved in
writing.
Attendance registers must be signed at each session; retrospective entries are not
accepted unless supported by a documented make up arrangement.
Instructors should retain practical demonstration checklists with trainee scores so
that assessment decisions can be reconstructed during audit.
Where a trainee misses an assessment, the coordinator records the reason and
schedules a retake within the published feedback window.
Monthly returns should reconcile trainee numbers with attendance records and flag
any unexplained difference for follow up.
The programme office compares site returns with central records and reports
discrepancies to the coordinator for correction.
Cost variances should be explained with reference to actual delivery activity rather
than assumed causes.
Equipment maintenance logs should be checked before each cohort to confirm that
practical sessions can proceed as planned.
Feedback from trainees is collected anonymously and summarised without
attributing comments to individuals.
Assessment rubrics must be applied consistently across sites; moderators compare a
sample of scored demonstrations each cycle.
Any change to the published timetable should be communicated to trainees
promptly and recorded in the monitoring log.

The risk log should be reviewed at each cohort meeting, with new risks added and
closed risks marked accordingly.
Figure 4: Reporting responsibilities and submission timeline
2.1.1.2 Variance Review and Corrective Action
Where an indicator deviates from plan, the site coordinator prepares a variance note
within 5 working days. The note states the observed deviation, the evidence
available and the proposed corrective action. Corrective actions are assigned an
owner and a closure date and are tracked in the monitoring log. Actions that require
additional expenditure must be approved before commitment, and unresolved
variances are reported to the programme board.
2.1.2 Reporting Timelines and Responsibilities
Site coordinators submit monthly returns by the published deadline, and the
programme office consolidates them into the cycle report. Instructors supply session
and assessment data; coordinators verify it; the office reviews it. Late or incomplete
returns are logged and followed up within 2 working days. The cycle report is
circulated to the programme board and retained with the supporting records for
audit purposes.
2.2 Implementation Risks and Escalation
Principal risks include instructor shortages, equipment failure and low trainee
attendance. Each site maintains a risk log and reviews it at every cohort meeting.
Risks that threaten delivery of the full 48 teaching hours are escalated immediately
to the programme office. Escalation includes the observed issue, its likely impact
and the proposed response. The office decides whether to adjust the schedule,
reallocate resources or pause the affected cohort.
